name: Illinois Brick Co. v. Illinois
summary: The Supreme Court held that only direct purchasers—not indirect purchasers—may sue for damages under federal antitrust law, establishing clear limits on antitrust standing that Congress and courts have carefully calibrated.
significance: Cited by Apple to illustrate that federal antitrust law has carefully constructed rules about who can sue and for what, and that state law should not be used to circumvent those federal policy choices.
